title: Rational interval tangent certificate and nearest axis-frozen finite-channel boundary discriminator

certified_domain.base_seed: u is the unique root of 17u^3-38u^2+84u-24 in the recorded rational interval; uniqueness follows because 51u^2-76u+84 has negative discriminant and positive leading coefficient.
certified_domain.section: The first-order K1738 truncation p*=p0+P/32, a*=a0+A/32 at s=1/32 and q=s^2=1/1024.
certified_domain.boundary_slice: Axis-frozen vertical slice p=p*. On this slice u=q has lower intercept a_sing=1-sqrt((2-q)(1-p*)/p*).

certified_conclusion.leading_velocity: The K1738 Jacobian is strictly positive on the isolated seed box and its selected P,A boxes are replayed by outward rational arithmetic.
certified_conclusion.exact_tangent_comparison: The K1728 fixed-raw-radii tangent has xi in [730.941507691374,730.941509424213], hence pays exact q^5 coefficient excess xi^2/5040 in [106.007041203,106.007041707]. This is an asymptotic coefficient theorem, not a finite-q integral ordering.
certified_conclusion.finite_channel_boundary: At q=1/1024 the K1738 linear truncation has u*>q. Holding p=p*, its lower u=q intercept is only 0.055450061994..0.055450062004 below a*, strictly closer in that same axis-frozen comparison than every rectangular chart face; the next closest listed face is p=1 at gap 0.160444186038..0.160444186042.
certified_conclusion.route_change: A future whole-chart certificate must treat the u=q singular face explicitly before remote p=1 support escape; a compact interior box around the K1738 branch alone cannot exclude the nearest axis-frozen competitor seam.

ordinary_floating_regression.interpretation: The two quadrature orders reproduce the expected ordering, but agreement between floating orders does not bound quadrature error and does not prove the finite-strength ordering.

finite_strength_interval_boundary.why: The Fisher objective contains exponentials, posterior ratios and a whole-line Gaussian integral. Fraction arithmetic certifies the algebraic chart but cannot enclose those transcendental integrals or their tails.
finite_strength_interval_boundary.missing_dependency: python-flint==0.9.0 (Arb), plus an implemented certified whole-line quadrature and Gaussian-tail enclosure
finite_strength_interval_boundary.next_exact_input: Install the repository-pinned optional Arb backend, derive a positive-denominator integrand form, split a compact y interval from two analytic Gaussian tails, and interval-branch the compact two-radius domain with a dedicated u=q boundary chart.

post_flight.overclaim_attack: Rejected: the 1.06e-13 floating objective gap is not relabeled as a theorem, and the exact xi^2/5040 result is not relabeled as finite-strength ordering.
post_flight.contrary_construction_or_mistyping_attac: The certificate derives the K1728 beta from its chart direction rather than trusting the printed decimal; hostile tests reject zero Jacobian, zero excess, swapped proof grades, false global decisions and an enlarged singular gap.
post_flight.reproducibility_seam: All proof-grade endpoints replay with the standard-library Fraction backend. Floating values replay through the pre-existing K1733 scipy backend and remain separately graded. The exact missing optional dependency and tail construction are named for continuation.

scope_guard: The boundary statement is axis-frozen at p=p* and compares a vertical singular intercept with rectangular coordinate-face gaps. It is not a global Euclidean nearest-boundary theorem. The linear truncation is not a proved continuation branch. No finite-strength Fisher interval ordering, whole-chart exclusion, global two-radius optimizer, all-seed result, growing-support exclusion, source-owned action, physical state, prediction or confirmation follows.
